questions.q:
In an aqueous solution, the ionization constants for carbonic acid are

${K}_{1} = \text{4.2} \times 1 {0}^{- 7}$ and ${ K}_{2} = \text{4.8} \times 1 {0}^{- 11}$

Select the correct statement for a saturated $\text{0.034 M}$ solution of the carbonic acid:
options: The concentration of $H^{+}$ is double that of ${CO}_{3}^{2 -}$.
The concentration of ${CO}_{3}^{2 -}$ is greater than that of ${HCO}_{3}^{-}$.
The concentration of $H^{+}$ and ${HCO}_{3}^{-}$ are approximately equal.
questions.solution:
$\begin{cases}{H}_{2} {CO}_{3} & ⇌ & H^{+} & + & {HCO}_{3}^{-} \text{;} & {K}_{1} & = & \text{4.2} \times 1 {0}^{- 7} \\ {HCO}_{3}^{-} & ⇌ & H^{+} & + & {CO}_{3}^{2 -} \text{;} & {K}_{2} & = & \text{4.8} \times 1 {0}^{- 1 1}\end{cases}$

$∵ {K}_{1} ≫ {K}_{2}$, so ${H}_{2} {CO}_{3}$ ionises more than ${HCO}_{3}^{-}$ and hence, contribution of $H^{+}$ is mostly due to ionization of carbonic acid. Thus, the concentrations of $H^{+}$ and ${HCO}_{3}^{-}$ are approximately equal.

${\text{pK}_{b} \text{of}{\text{CN}^{−} = 4.69 ∴ {\text{pK}_{\text{HCN}} = 9.31; {K}_{\text{HCN}} = 4.9 \times {10}^{- 10}$

${pK}_{{CH}_{3} \text{COOH}} = \text{4.75} ; {K}_{{CH}_{3} \text{COOH}} = \text{1.77} \times 1 {0}^{- 5}$

questions.q: K_{a} for HCN is 5 x 10^{- 10} at 25^{o} C. For maintaining a constant pH of 9, the volume of 5 M KCN solution required to be added to 10 mL of 2 M HCN solution is:
questions.solution:
On mixing the given solutions, acidic buffer will be formed. Thus applying Henderson equation to find the pH-

$pH = {pK}_{a} + \log_{10}\dfrac{[ {CN}^{-} ]}{[ HCN ]}$

$\text{pH} = - \text\log 5 \times 1 {0}^{- 1 0} + \text\log \dfrac{5 \times \text{V} / \text{V} + 1 0}{1 0 \times 2 / \text{V} + 1 0}$

$9 = - \text\log 5 \times 1 {0}^{- 1 0} + \text\log \dfrac{\text{V}}{4}$

$9 = 1 0 - 0 \text{.} 7 + \text\log \dfrac{\text{V}}{4}$

$- 0 \text{.} 3 = \text\log \dfrac{\text{V}}{4}$

$∴\text\log \dfrac{\text{V}}{4} {=}^{-} 0 \text{.} 3 = \text\log \dfrac{1}{2}$

& $\dfrac{\text{V}}{4} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$∴$ V = 2 mL.

Suppose S is the molar solubility of silver benzoate in water, then

${K}_{sp} = S{′}^{2}\left[\dfrac{{K}_{a}}{{K}_{a} + \left[{H}^{+}\right]}\right]$

$S′ = {\left\{\dfrac{2.5 \times 1{0}^{- 13} \times 7.106 \times 1{0}^{- 4}}{6.46 \times 1{0}^{- 5}}\right\}}^{\dfrac{1}{2}}$

Silver benzoate is 3.32 times more soluble in buffer of pH = 3.19 than in pure water.
